items.title: Scaffold the api service so real build, test and lint run in CI
items.outcome: The api repository contains a buildable Ktor service with a real test task and a real lint task, so the CI policy that already requires build, test and lint stops being a green light over an empty repository.
items.context: Every component repository currently holds only a README while CI claims to enforce language-specific build, test and lint. The claim is unfalsifiable and hides the fact that no repository can actually run a pipeline. This ticket makes the api pipeline honest and gives every later api ticket a place to land. This scaffold is dependency-free by design: the CI conformance gate depends on it, not the other way round, so it can start in Sprint 01 alongside every other scaffold.
scope: Gradle build with the agreed Kotlin and Ktor versions and a reproducible lock
Application entry point, configuration loading and a health endpoint
Test source set with one meaningful passing test and a coverage report task
Formatter and static analysis configuration wired into the build
Dockerfile and local run instructions consistent with the compose environment
acceptance_criteria: A clean clone builds, tests and lints with the documented commands and no manual setup
The health endpoint returns a machine-readable readiness and liveness result
A deliberately introduced formatting or lint violation fails the build
A deliberately failing test fails the pipeline rather than being skipped
The service image starts against the compose environment and reports ready
contracts_schema: Health response schema published in the repository and referenced by the deploy readiness probe
Configuration keys documented with type, default and whether they are required
security_privacy: No credentials committed; configuration is read from the environment only
The health endpoint exposes no version-disclosing or tenant-identifying data
observability: Startup and readiness logged as structured events with no request payloads
Build duration and test count published as pipeline metrics
tests: Unit test on configuration loading including a missing-required-key failure
Pipeline self-test that asserts the lint and test gates actually fail on planted defects
rollout_rollback: Merged directly to main behind branch protection; no runtime feature flag needed
Rollback is a revert of the scaffold commit, which cannot affect user data
non_goals: Domain logic, persistence schema and authentication, which belong to their own tickets
Deployment infrastructure, which belongs to E24

items.title: Scaffold the contracts repository with spec lint, code generation and publishing
items.outcome: The contracts repository can lint the OpenAPI document, generate Kotlin, TypeScript and Python clients and publish them, so every consumer repository - including the Python ai-service - gets its client from one reproducible pipeline.
items.context: Client generation is assumed by the api, android and web plans but no repository owns it. Without a pipeline the generated clients drift silently and the contract stops being authoritative. This scaffold is dependency-free by design: the CI conformance gate depends on it, not the other way round, so it can start in Sprint 01 alongside every other scaffold.
scope: Specification linting with an agreed rule set and a failing exit code
Kotlin, TypeScript and Python client generation with pinned generator versions
Versioned publication of generated artifacts consumable by the other repositories
Backwards-compatibility diff against the previously published specification
acceptance_criteria: A malformed specification fails the pipeline with an actionable message
Generated clients compile or import cleanly in a smoke consumer project for all three target languages, including a Python smoke consumer that type-checks
A breaking specification change is detected and fails the pull request unless explicitly acknowledged
Regenerating from an unchanged specification produces byte-identical output
The Python client exposes the money type as a Decimal-backed wrapper with its currency and never as a float, proven by a smoke test that rejects float construction
contracts_schema: OpenAPI 3.1 document is the single source of truth; generator configuration is committed
Published artifact coordinates and versioning scheme documented
Generator configuration pins one generator version per target language, and the Python target is a first-class output rather than a convenience script
security_privacy: No secrets in generator configuration; publishing uses short-lived federated credentials
Generated clients contain no example data derived from real records
observability: Pipeline publishes the specification version and generator version with each artifact
tests: Generator determinism test
Breaking-change detection test with a planted removal
Python client import and type-check test in the smoke consumer
rollout_rollback: Additive specification changes publish automatically; breaking changes require the expand and contract protocol
Rollback is republishing the previous artifact version, which consumers pin explicitly
non_goals: Adding new endpoints, which belongs to the contract expansion tickets

scope: Synthetic demonstration data applied through the migration runner T-MIG-01 owns, never through a second ad hoc apply path

Seed command that is idempotent and refuses to run against a non-development database

items.title: Build the schema migration runner, registry integration and reversal evidence
items.outcome: Every schema change in the api repository is applied by one runner that records it in the migration registry, refuses a second in-flight migration, and produces reversal evidence, so the first real migration - the ledger schema - lands under the protocol rather than ahead of it.
items.context: The ledger schema in api#2 is the first migration this system applies, and it is the one migration nobody can afford to get wrong. Today the runner is bundled into T-ENV-01 in Sprint 07, four sprints after the schema it is supposed to apply, and T-GOV-04's migration registry and lock have nothing on the api side to integrate with. This ticket pulls the runner in front of api#2 and gives it a single owner, so the seeding ticket owns seed data only.
scope: Migration runner wired into the api build and into continuous integration, with forward and reverse for every change
Expand-migrate-contract sequencing support so a migration can deploy ahead of the code that uses it
Integration with the T-GOV-04 migration registry and lock: claim, release, and refusal when another migration is in flight
Reversal evidence produced per migration: either a rehearsed down migration or a named compensating migration with the reason the reverse is impossible
Naming, ordering and checksum convention so a migration edited after it has been applied is detected
Dry-run mode that prints the plan and writes nothing
Documented recovery path for a migration that fails part-way
acceptance_criteria: Every migration applies forward and reverses cleanly on an empty database and on a populated database, run in continuous integration
A migration whose checksum changed after it was applied fails the run and names the file
Starting a second migration while one holds the registry lock fails, and the message names the lock holder
A migration merged with neither a rehearsed reverse nor a named compensating migration fails the pull request
Dry-run mode writes nothing, proven by a test that asserts an unchanged schema version
A migration that fails part-way leaves the database at a known version and the documented recovery path is exercised in a test
api#2 applies its ledger schema through this runner; a second apply path in the api repository is a review failure
contracts_schema: Migration naming, ordering, checksum and reversibility convention published in the api repository and referenced by every schema ticket
Registry claim and release payload shared with T-GOV-04, so the lock the pull request check reads is the lock the runner takes
security_privacy: The runner uses a migration role distinct from the runtime application role, and the runtime role is never granted schema-change rights
Migration output redacts row values; a failure message names the constraint and the table, never the data
observability: Current schema version, last applied migration and lock holder are all readable without a database session
A migration that runs longer than the published threshold raises an alert rather than being discovered by a timeout elsewhere
tests: Round-trip test applying and reverting every migration
Checksum-drift detection test
Concurrent-lock refusal test naming the holder
Part-way failure and documented recovery test
Dry-run no-write test
rollout_rollback: The runner lands before the first schema ticket, so no migration is ever applied outside it
Rollback is reverting the runner and, because no migration has been applied through it yet at that point, no data change to unwind
non_goals: Seed and demonstration data, which T-ENV-01 owns
The pull request check that enforces one in-flight migration, which T-GOV-04 owns; this ticket provides the runner side of that lock
Schema content, which each schema ticket owns
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo api. Solely owns the migration runner, the registry client and the reversal-evidence rule. T-GOV-04 owns the pull request check that reads the registry; T-ENV-01 owns seed data and applies it through this runner.

items.title: Publish the shared client state and copy taxonomy for every non-happy path
items.outcome: Android, web and admin share one named vocabulary for empty, loading, error, offline, stale, permission-denied, quota-exceeded and degraded states, with the copy rules and the recovery action for each, so the client quality gates can assert coverage rather than taste.
items.context: Every client ticket lists its own non-happy-path states in its own words, so the same condition is called offline in one ticket, stale in another and error in a third. That makes the client quality gates unenforceable: a gate cannot assert a screen handles offline if offline has no definition. It also produces user-visible inconsistency in exactly the situations where trust is thinnest - a permission denial, a failed sync, an exhausted quota.
scope: Named state taxonomy: empty, loading, error, offline, stale, permission-denied, quota-exceeded, degraded, each with a definition and the condition that produces it
Per state: what the surface must show, what it must not show, whether the underlying data may still be displayed, and the single recovery action offered
Copy rules per state, including the rule that a state never blames the user and never invents a cause
Stale versus offline distinction: how a surface signals data it has but cannot refresh
Degraded distinction: a dependency is unavailable but the surface is still useful, versus an error where it is not
Machine-readable state identifiers that client tests and the quality gates assert against
Worked examples for the three highest-risk surfaces: a permission-denied capture surface, a quota-exceeded AI surface and a stale shared balance
acceptance_criteria: Every state in the taxonomy has a definition, a triggering condition, required and forbidden content, and exactly one recovery action
The taxonomy distinguishes offline from stale and error from degraded, and states the observable difference a user sees between each pair
The state identifiers are published as machine-readable data, so a client test asserts an identifier rather than a string
The copy rules forbid blaming the user, forbid inventing a cause the client cannot know, and require the same wording for the same state across clients
A permission-denied state is specified to keep the rest of the surface usable, consistent with the rule that the app is fully usable with every permission denied
A quota-exceeded state is specified to state what is still available rather than only what is blocked
Three worked examples are published, one per named high-risk surface
contracts_schema: State identifier vocabulary published as machine-readable data in the docs repository, referenced by the client quality gates
Names which identifiers correspond to contract-level conditions, such as an entitlement deny or a revoked grant, so a client state maps to a real API result
security_privacy: Error and degraded copy must not leak internal identifiers, stack detail or another user's existence
A permission-denied state must not reveal whether data exists behind the denial
observability: Each state identifier names the client signal that records it, so the frequency of each non-happy path is measurable rather than anecdotal
tests: Names the coverage assertion the client quality gates run: every listed surface handles every applicable state identifier
Review test that a new state cannot be added to a client without adding it to the taxonomy first
rollout_rollback: Published once as documentation and data; clients adopt it as their surfaces are built
Rollback is reverting the document, which leaves the clients with their existing per-ticket wording
non_goals: Visual design, component library or theming
Localisation of the copy, which E30 owns
Implementing any state in any client
